title: Read it back
note: Karima al-Marwaziyya and the ijazah: verified transmission.

research.quotes: heroes.html#karima-al-marwaziyya: 'she made them collate. A student's manuscript had to be read back against her own verified original, error by error, before she would certify it with her ijazah, her formal license to transmit.' 'She died in Makkah around 1070 CE, close to a hundred years old, having spent perhaps half a century as a living checkpoint.' 'some classical chains of the Sahih recited in mosques pass through her name.' Person meta line: 'Karima al-Marwaziyya, around 975 to 1070 CE · Merv, then Makkah.'
research.retell: A scholar named Karima al-Marwaziyya spent about fifty years in Makkah making students read their handwritten copies of a famous hadith book back to her out loud so she could catch every mistake before she would sign off on them.

lines.text: One woman checked every copy by ear
lines.sub: every copy read back, out loud, line by line

lines.text: Karima holds the most trusted copy
lines.sub: the most checked book after the Qur'an

lines.text: Copying by hand lets errors creep in
So you read yours back to her
lines.sub: out loud, checked line by line

lines.text: One error caught is one error stopped
Only then does she sign your licence

lines.sub: the hadith you hear still pass through her

lines.text: She died in Makkah, near a hundred
